hints.title: Prime Base Divisibility
hints.text: Three is a prime number, meaning any integer power of three can only be divided by lower powers of three. Can a single divisibility check test for powers of three?

hints.title: Upper Limit Constant Invariant
hints.text: The largest power of three that fits inside a thirty-two bit signed integer is three to the nineteenth power, which equals 1162261467.

hints.title: Direct Modulo Evaluation Procedure
hints.text: Ensure n is strictly positive. Check whether 1162261467 modulo n equals zero. Because three is prime, any integer divisor of this maximum power must itself be a power of three.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Looping division or conversion to base-3 strings takes O(log3 N) time and can suffer from floating point inaccuracies when using logarithms.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single modulo operation against the maximum 32-bit power of three runs in O(1) time and O(1) space with absolute arithmetic precision.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain why this constant upper bound modulo trick works exclusively for prime bases.
